business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Swiss Confederation (Eidgenossenschaft), comprising 26 cantons with cantonal commercial registries operating as decentralized units under federal law
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations, Civil Code, and Federal Acts) with a strong tradition of direct democracy and neo-corporatist regulatory practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 16 November 1986, entered into force 17 March 1987)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 25 September 2013, entered into force 12 September 2014)
Agreement between Switzerland and the European Union on Free Trade and Trade-Related Matters (1972, with successive updates under the bilateral agreements)
Switzerland–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 1951, as amended by protocols, most recently 1996 and 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (GwG/LBA, SR 951.0) and its implementing ordinances; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Art. 305bis (criminal money laundering) and Art. 305ter (defective financial transactions); Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 620 et seq. on Aktiengesellschaft; Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 926–927 on the Register of Beneficial Owners as introduced by the Federal Act of 16 December 2022 on the Register of Beneficial Owners, in force since 1 July 2024; FINMA Circular 2017/1 on AML/CFT supervision; SECO Economic Sanctions Ordinance (SR 946.201) and relevant UN/EU/OFAC sanctions lists

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy (with public deed) of the founder's official passport or national identity card (all non-Swiss signatories)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the country of origin (e.g., public registrar, national police, or diplomatic mission)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Either Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state OR consular legalization by the Swiss representation if the issuing state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign parent company or historic legal entity (if any) issued by the domestic company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign official company registry or commercial court

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and translated copy of the original foreign board resolutions authorizing the Swiss incorporation and identifying beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate secretary and/or notary public; official translation certified by Swiss court or Federal Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization (for the underlying corporate document); Swiss certified translation not subjected to apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified banking references for the beneficial owner(s) evidencing lawful origin of funds for the CHF 100,000 share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the beneficial owner in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization (if required by the Swiss notary; otherwise bank letter authentication under Swiss AML practice)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Swiss due-diligence questionnaire (KYC form) with personal data of each UBO (name, date of birth, nationality, residence, proof of source of wealth)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The appointed Swiss licensed legal professional / fiduciary acting as company formation agent; completed by the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Autograph signature before the Swiss notary OR notarial authentication in the country of residence followed by Apostille/consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of all shareholders, directors, representatives, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and signatories against the United Nations Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN List, Swiss SECO sanctions list, Swiss FINMA enforcement list, and the Interpol Red Notice database. Enhanced due diligence is required for any person resident in or connected to sanctioned jurisdictions, and for defense-sector high-risk activity. For ISIC 3040 (military tactical vehicles), screening frequency must be continuous (event-driven) and at minimum quarterly. A risk-based justification and contemporaneous evidence must be retained for a minimum of 10 years under Art. 13 GwG. Any positive PEP designation triggers enhanced monitoring, senior management approval, and mandatory reporting to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) in accordance with GwG.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex – ZEFIX), operated by the Swiss Federal Office of Justice (BJ) in collaboration with the 26 cantonal commercial register offices; initial pre-clearance may be obtained through the Hellenic? no, through the cantonal commercial register portal (e.g., Zefix report) and final registration must be filed with the competent cantonal registry (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug for the Zug cH financial cluster)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in a state language of Switzerland (German, French, or Italian; Romansh permitted only in canton Grisons) or an accepted transliteration/translation of the foreign concept. The name must not be misleading, offensive, or infringe on well-known third-party trade marks. The approved suffix indicating Aktiengesellschaft must match the corporate language: 'AG' (German), 'SA' (French), 'Ltd', or 'PLC' is not permitted for a Swiss AG; the Italian 'SA' is also accepted. A non-Latin script name is not registrable; the Latin-alphabet transliteration must be approved and the original script must be clearly indicated in the registry entry. The registry will reject a name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or to names protected under the Swiss Federal Industrial Design Act or Trade Mark Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name request (Voreintragungsgesuch) may be submitted via the cantonal register office; if the requested name is not rejected within 30 days, provisional reservation may be extended under manual evaluation. In case of a formal rejection, the applicant may within 60 days file a written objection with the supervising cantonal authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehörde) under Art. 940 OR and Sections 93–95 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV). If the objection is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the cantonal administrative court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of notification, and finally to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court on grounds of violation of federal law. The refusal must be communicated with the statutory reasoning, and the applicant is entitled to inspect the conflicting registry entries to assess whether a modification of the corporate name would satisfy the Registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements (shared business address, mailbox-only services, or remote no-physical-presence solutions) are generally unacceptable as the registered office of a Swiss AG for defense-sector activities. The statutory registered office must be a physical premise located in the canton designated in the articles of incorporation, with actual business operations and records accessible. For an ISIC 3040 military tactical vehicle manufacturer, the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS), armasuisse, and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) mandate a permanent local subsidiary with a fixed place of business, adequate floor space, full-time management, and accessible procurement and export documentation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial act for public deed of incorporation (constitution, articles of association, and UBO declaration) drafted before a Swiss notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary chamber and Swiss notary fees under the cantonal Notariatsgebührenverordnung (tariff varies by canton, benchmark for Zug/Zurich between CHF 2,500 and CHF 4,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee for the incorporation of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, including preliminary name check and final entry in the canton's register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) pursuant to SR 221.411.1 (Commercial Register Fee Ordinance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO-R) initial disclosure filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Office of Justice (BJ), General Collection of the Confederation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee (Regulatory Federal Ordinance on the Register of Beneficial Owners)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Disclosure and screening against Swiss SECO Economic Sanctions, UN and EU sanctions lists performed by licensed AML compliance provider, including OFAC SDN screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: The appointed AML/CFT compliance provider subject to FINMA supervision (market benchmark for a defense-sector due-diligence package)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on the compatibility of the corporate objects (manufacture of all-terrain military tactical vehicles) with Swiss law, war-matériel legislation, and the dual-use regulation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Swiss commercial law firm or law firm with listed war material license expertise
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark and professional hourly fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille authentication and/or consular legalization of foreign founder documents (passport copies, parent company registry extract, UBO due-diligence forms) at the competent cantonal office or Swiss consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA) and/or the competent foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs (depending on apostille or consular route), charged per document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee schedule (Gebührenverordnung EDA) and foreign authority fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank certificate of paid-up capital and escrow/blocked account administration fee for the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital (APC process)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss cantonal bank or FINMA-registered commercial bank where the founder's capital contribution is held; fee per bank's general terms and conditions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation of corporate documentation (articles of association, UBO forms, due dossiers) into the official language of the cantonal register (German, French, or Italian) by a court-approved translator, with written certificates of translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation service appointed by the notary; fee in accordance with Swiss translation associations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–763; Arts. 629–632 on incorporation and paid-up capital; Art. 640 on registered shares; Arts. 698, 707 and 716a on board duties; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Arts. 2, 18–43.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug), supported by the federal Zefix and eGRIS electronic registries.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted to the commercial register by a sworn notary through eGRIS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: AG minimum share capital is CHF 100,000. At least CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash and deposited into a blocked Swiss bank account (Sperrkonto) before registration. In-kind contributions require an audit report and do not satisfy the blocked-cash deposit requirement; any issue premium must be fully paid in.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation instruments and the subscription of 100 registered shares, each with CHF 1,000 nominal value and aggregate share capital of CHF 100,000, be ratified; the required paid-up capital has been deposited as required by Article 632 OR. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established in Zug, Switzerland, with effective domicile and records at that address. RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors shall consist of three members, with [Name A] appointed Chairperson, [Name B] appointed Vice-Chairperson, and [Name C] appointed Member. RESOLVED, that [Name D], a licensed expert auditor, be appointed statutory auditor. RESOLVED, that management be instructed to submit the commercial-register filing and secure all defense and environmental permits before commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Zefix portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter the proposed corporate name 'CH AG' and legal form 'Aktiengesellschaft' into Zefix; verify that no identical or confusingly similar name exists; obtain name clearance and confirm the statutory seat in the Canton of Zug.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Association draft
Identity documents of incorporators
Completed name reservation form
Declaration of Swiss domicile for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts, file an administrative objection with the registry, withdraw the original reservation and resubmit with a disclaimed or modified corporate name within the standard processing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of incorporation deed and statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with final statutes; verify initial capital, board composition, auditor, registered office and beneficial ownership; have the deed read and signed; the notary retains the instrument for submission to the commercial register after capital payment.
required_dossiers: Shareholder incorporation instructions
Final Articles of Association in German
Passports or identity documents of all shareholders and board members
Notary engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For formal or translation defects, execute a notarial correction amendment (Nachtrag) before the same notary and re-attach it to the original incorporation deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocked bank account and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or a qualified private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the company name; deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash; obtain and deliver the bank's blocked-account confirmation for registration; after legal personality is granted, obtain the bank release instruction for operational use.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed
Draft commercial register application
Beneficial ownership declaration
AML/KYC questionnaires for shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects source-of-funds documentation, provide audited statements or notarized gift and funding declarations and resubmit; if the bank remains unsatisfied, terminate and reopen the account at another licensed Swiss bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register submission and issuance of legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / eGRIS electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the electronic registration with executed statutes, board list, capital payment confirmation, auditor consent and authorized signatory specimen forms. The registry examines formal compliance; upon acceptance the company is entered in the commercial register and acquires legal personality, followed by publication in the Swiss Official Gazette.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed and Articles of Association
Blocked capital confirmation certificate from the bank
Signed board member and authorized signatory specimen forms
Statutory auditor declaration of acceptance
Commercial register fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction query (Beanstandung), respond within 30 days by submitting revised schedules, notarized ordinances or capital-evidence documents and expedite the refiling through the cantonal registry desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance organisation and officer powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Shareholders' Meeting of CH AG
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ratify the first board resolution; adopt organizational regulations; establish the share register, minutes ledger and signature matrix; ensure the statutory auditor has unrestricted inspection rights; record board delegations in the corporate records and notify the commercial register of any authorized representatives.
required_dossiers: First board resolutions
Organizational regulations (Organisationsreglement)
Share register and capital issuance records
Statutory auditor acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If governance or signature authorization is defective, convene a corrective board meeting and file amended resolutions with the commercial register before the company concludes binding transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SECO — State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, Goods Control Directorate; armasuisse security vetting partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the war-material manufacturing licence application under the Federal Act on War Material (Kriegsmaterialgesetz, KMG) and the goods-control operating authorization under the Goods Control Act (Güterkontrollgesetz, GKG). Include the technical file, plant location, physical security measures, beneficial ownership data, export-compliance program and official security screening consent.
required_dossiers: Application form for war-material manufacturing authorization
Commercial register excerpt of CH AG
Beneficial ownership chart and security documentation
Technical file of the all-terrain military tactical vehicle
Compliance program and internal control manual
Canton of Zug zoning and building permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SECO requests supplementary information, provide confidential technical declarations, update the product classification or initiate a pre-notification procedure; administrative appeal may be filed with the Federal Administrative Court within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU); Cantonal Environmental Office and Fire Inspectorate; SUVA — Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the full environmental impact assessment, obtain the environmental operating permit, install wastewater and emissions abatement equipment, secure the fire safety certificate, complete structural load inspection and undergo SUVA occupational health and safety clearance. Production may only commence after every clearance is granted.
required_dossiers: Full environmental impact assessment report
Site plans and environmental coordination documents
Fire safety concept and emergency escape plan
Structural engineer load calculation certification
Occupational health program and SUVA registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EIA conditions are challenged, submit a corrective action plan and technical design adjustments; if fire or occupational clearance is refused, implement remedial measures and request re-inspection by the responsible authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER) — SECO Goods Control Directorate, with armasuisse as the technical security vetting authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing and Operating Licence for War Material (Kriegsmaterialgesetz, KMG) and Controlled Goods Authorization (Güterkontrollgesetz, GKG)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) in coordination with the Canton of Zug environmental office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A — Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report required under Annex I of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfungsverordnung, UVPV) for defense equipment manufacturing facilities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater compliance with Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (Gewässerschutzverordnung) schedule 3.2, including limits for electroplating and metal-finishing discharges such as total chromium ≤ 0.5 mg/L, nickel ≤ 0.5 mg/L and COD ≤ 60 mg/L after treatment; VOC abatement per Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) and VOCV with exhaust gas VOC concentration not exceeding 20 mg C/m3 or solvent recovery efficiency of at least 98%; hazardous waste handling and manifest control under Special Waste Ordinance (Sonderabfallverordnung, SAdV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate based on a VKF-certified fire protection concept; structural load inspection certificate for production and assembly halls; SUVA workplace clearance and occupational health program approval for heavy tactical vehicle assembly operations; emergency response and civil defense plan for hazardous activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA), Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV), Swiss Confederation; online portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch with e-services at https://ses.estv.admin.ch and VAT-specific portal at https://www.vat.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Swiss company UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) through the central business register database (Zefix) using authenticated proof of incorporation and legal existence. For VAT liability, the foreign entity files Form 004 'Registration for VAT purposes' with the ESTV. A Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nummer) is issued where the entity supplies taxable goods or services in Switzerland and annual Swiss taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, or where the foreign business is nonetheless liable under Article 21 of the Swiss VAT Act. A non-resident AG with no Swiss seat may need to appoint a Swiss tax representative for VAT enforcement and correspondence. Direct tax registration for non-resident shareholders is limited to Swiss-source nexus; the AG itself is not required to obtain a separate income tax certificate for foreign tax residency, but transfer pricing and permanent establishment rules apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Swiss law. An Aktiengesellschaft is mandatorily taxed as a legal entity on its taxable profit at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Available elective or preferential mechanisms include Swiss VAT group treatment (Organschaft) through a control election, the participation exemption for qualified dividend and capital gains, the patent/IP box regime, notional interest deduction on shareholder loans, and the reimbursement of capital contribution reserves by means of tax-neutral repayment when properly documented. There is no hybrid mismatch check-the-box election; Swiss Federal Tax Administration circulars and the OECD-related GloBE rules govern controlled foreign company and hybrid instrument treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT; Mehrwertsteuer, TVA, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual turnover from taxable supplies connected with Switzerland (Article 21 paragraph 1 left Swiss VAT Act). Foreign suppliers with Swiss-source taxable turnover crossing this threshold must register; certain cross-border digital and electronic services may trigger Swiss VAT liability independent of a fixed domestic establishment, and a simplified registration procedure applies for foreign e-services providers with no Swiss establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or fiscal stamp mechanism. Registered taxable persons must issue bookable invoices containing statutory VAT elements; e-invoicing through Peppol, Swiss QR-bill, EDI, or XML is permitted. For domestic payments the Swiss QR-bill with embedded QR code replaces traditional payment slips. VAT returns must be submitted electronically through the ESTV portal on a quarterly or semi-annual basis. No government API mandate for transaction-level data extraction is in force for B2B, but the ESTV may require access to accounting records during an audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for the 0% VAT rate where the supplier proves that the goods were physically transported from Switzerland to a foreign destination, are delivered to a foreign buyer, and the customs export declaration is accepted by Swiss Customs. For military tactical vehicles and defense hardware, zero rating applies only if the goods are lawfully exported under the applicable war material or goods control license issued by SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs). Offshore services supplied by a Swiss exporter to a foreign recipient are zero-rated where the service recipient is abroad and the service is actually used or exploited outside Switzerland; services directly connected with exported goods (freight, insurance, logistics) also qualify. The zero-rating claim must be evidenced contemporaneously.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of export release by Swiss Customs (Ausfuhrschein / export voucher)
Transport documents (air waybill, CMR, or rail waybill)
Certificate of foreign import approval or end-user certificate for military controlled goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export documentation is insufficient, unauthentic, or incomplete, the ESTV will re-assess VAT at the standard rate of 8.1% with default interest from due date. Retrospective clawback extends to an assessment period usually governed by the 5-year VAT limitation, extending to 10 years in cases of tax fraud or misrepresentation. Claiming zero-rating on fictitious or non-exported goods constitutes tax evasion under the Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law, punishable by fines of up to CHF 10,000 for simple offences; for fraudulent export with intent, imprisonment up to three years or monetary penalty up to three times the evaded tax may be imposed. Input VAT deduction is reversed correlatively, and the customs authorities may additionally impose penalties under the Customs Act. Although Switzerland has no statutory inward-remittance deadline for VAT zero-rating, a 180-day commercial benchmark for export payment reconciliation is used in practice to support beneficial ownership and transfer-pricing documentation; delayed repatriation alone does not immediately deny zero-rating but may trigger arm's-length adjustment if retained abroad without commercial justification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank, SNB) — primary monetary, currency, and financial-stability authority; the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) administers Swiss war-material and dual-use export-control licensing, but retains no foreign-exchange control function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible; there are no exchange-control laws, no prior approval requirements, no currency-quantity limits, and no mandatory conversion requirements for cross-border capital movements or profit distributions. Profit remittance is unrestricted for Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, subject only to solvency tests and statutory balance-sheet protections under the Swiss Code of Obligations. Sanctions screening, AML checks, and FINMA KYC obligations remain applicable to all inbound and outbound transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules exist in Switzerland. Exporters are not required to repatriate export proceeds within any timeline, nor are they required to convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. Exporters may retain or freely convert proceeds through authorized Swiss banks or hedge them in the foreign-exchange market. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations apply, executed by banks through the Swiss National Bank's reporting framework.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for a defense-tactical-hardware manufacturer. Offshore digital EMIs are not recognized as Swiss banks and generally lack FINMA authorization to take deposits or operate full payment-account services in Switzerland. Such EMIs routinely reject high-risk defense-sector clients because of sanctions exposure, export-control sensitivity, and AML enhancements. A Swiss fintech license under FINMA would be feasible only for niche payment services but would not replace the compliance and clearing capacity of a regulated Swiss bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory. Swiss banks require an in-person interview at a Swiss branch for high-risk corporate clients, which necessarily includes ultimate beneficial owners and statutory signatories. Remote video identification is permitted only under FINMA-compliant procedures for lower-risk clients. Banks reserve complete discretion to demand physical appearance, notarized corporate documents, and a personally conducted source-of-wealth interview before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive UN/EU/Swiss/OFAC sanctions-screening report, ultimate beneficial ownership chart, negative media-search report, board resolution on sanctions compliance, and validated customer and end-user screening lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use or war-material export control red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SECO war-material export authorization or dual-use license, end-user certificate, delivery-verification documentation, compliance manual under Swiss War Materials Control Act, and internal export-compliance officer declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the last three years, shareholder register and beneficial-owner declarations, source-of-funds documentation for capital injection, AML/KYC policies, and two independent bank or business references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ownership and control structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug), BORIS-registered legal-entity data, passport copies and proof of address for all UBOs, corporate-structure diagrams, and powers of attorney with precise signatory authority definitions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contribution must be routed through a FINMA-authorised Swiss bank using SWIFT MT103, with IBAN/BIC confirmation and the payment narrative clearly identifying 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection' plus a contractual reference. KYC verification includes source-of-funds documentation, a board resolution approving the injection, and the Swiss Commercial Register excerpt evidencing the share capital context. No Swiss exchange-control approval is required; banks will sanction-screen the originating parties and may request corporate documents before crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Export disbursements for tactical vehicles and spare parts are executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct settlement, or through documentary trade instruments such as commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600, including government and diplomatic LC structures with optional confirmation by a first-class Swiss or foreign bank. Defense-related outbound payments require prior SECO export authorization, end-user documentation, and delivery-compliance verification embedded in the export transaction file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible defense-trade counterpart currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and statutory audit report filing (if audit required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (December 31 for calendar-year companies) for shareholder approval; filing with the commercial register within 30 days after approval, not exceeding July 30 for calendar-year filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cantonal registry warnings and monetary penalties (typically CHF 100–1,000); persistent non-filing results in administrative strike-off of the company after formal notices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal, and municipal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonssteueramt) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus six months (April 30 for calendar-year companies); automatic extension of one to three months may be granted upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment with penalty interest (3.5% per annum for federal tax and 4%–4.5% for cantonal tax); administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 for willful failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if quarterly or semi-annual filing not applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the fiscal year-end (March 1 for calendar-year companies if annual filing is granted).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CHF 1,000–10,000 plus default interest at 4% per annum; repeated violations may trigger a safety deposit requirement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (Arts. 727–727b OR) is mandatory for Aktiengesellschaft if, for two consecutive financial years, any one of the following thresholds is exceeded: balance-sheet total CHF 3,000,000; annual revenue CHF 6,000,000; 10 full-time employees on average. This defense-manufacturing entity is presumed to exceed these thresholds and therefore requires an independent statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) and Swiss GAAP (Fachempfehlungen zur Rechnungslegung – FER) for statutory financial statements; IFRS required if the company is publicly listed. Military-contract-related special accounting directives may additionally apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), the company must maintain a register of beneficial owners and review it annually. No public filing is required, but the register must be made available to the Federal Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) and other competent authorities upon request. Any transfer of shares that changes beneficial ownership must be recorded within 14 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch / Register of Shareholders)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 3,000 per year for a licensed corporate service provider, including registered office address and standard secretarial support in Zug or Zurich.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 25,000 per year, reflecting defense-sector complexity, third-party audit review, and potential government-led oversight of military-vehicle manufacturing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct tax, plus cantonal and municipal profit tax resulting in a combined effective headline rate of 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box deduction abating up to 90% of qualifying IP income; R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of eligible research expenditure; notional interest deduction on excess taxable equity; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on substantial shareholdings

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined Cantonal and Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (e.g., Canton Zug Form M 30 for legal entities), filed through the respective cantonal e-filing portal (eTaxport) or the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) e-services for federal tax coordination
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the calendar year following the financial year end, extendable to 30 September, and in justified cases to 31 December, upon written application to the cantonal tax administration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue from manufacture and supply of all-terrain military tactical vehicles and spare parts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must include only Swiss-source revenue attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment; defense export licenses under the Federal Act on War Material must be referenced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before income tax per Swiss statutory financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for Swiss tax law differences, including disproportional financing costs and arm's-length transfer pricing corrections for related-party defense procurement transactions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption deduction on qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable for Swiss-resident AGs or Swiss permanent establishments; attach a schedule of qualified holdings and proof of economic substance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable Swiss withholding tax (35%) on Swiss-source dividend, interest, and royalty income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must attach proof of beneficial ownership and the applicable DTA relief form; refund is processed through ESTV Form 82

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit and capital tax base after all statutory deductions and tax incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident military exporters may not claim treaty or federal incentives unless they maintain a Swiss permanent establishment and satisfy the effective place of management test

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to procedural orders with administrative fines up to CHF 10,000, default interest at 4% per annum, and a cumulative late-filing surcharge of up to 3% of assessed tax; willful failure can result in criminal tax proceedings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Swiss AG withholds 35% on dividends paid to non-residents; the beneficial owner applies for reduction or refund under the applicable DTA by submitting the Swiss withholding tax reclaim (Form 82/82a) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, accompanied by an official residency certificate (Form 823) plus documentary evidence of beneficial ownership and absence of abusive holding structures
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest from Swiss bonds and qualifying receivables is 35%; arm's-length royalty payments generally escape statutory Swiss withholding tax, but a 35% anti-abuse withholding may apply to royalties paid to affiliated beneficiaries in non-cooperative jurisdictions without entitlement to DTA relief; applicable treaty rates on interest and royalties range from 0% to 10%

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and, where applicable, Master File are required when the Swiss entity's gross sales exceed CHF 50,000,000 or cross-border related-party transactions in any category exceed CHF 1,000,000 annually; below these thresholds, a simplified contemporaneous arm's-length analysis must still be maintained
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies an economic substance principle through the federal general anti-abuse rule (Art. 21 DBG), the effective place of management doctrine, and participation-exemption substance criteria; a manufacturer of all-terrain military tactical vehicles must demonstrate actual operational substance, including production facilities, engineering staffing, board decisions in Switzerland, and import/export authorization; purely passive letterbox entities are disregarded and denied treaty benefits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional understatement of profit from sales of all-terrain military tactical vehicles to foreign government buyers through fictitious invoicing, phantom costs, or unreported cash-connected transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years; civil administrative fine up to 50%–100% of the understated tax; final tax assessment reopened without limitation period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax plus interest; personal asset seizure, Swiss travel ban, and imprisonment of up to 3 years for knowing signature of false tax declarations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG as a shell intermediary that licenses defense IP from a zero-tax related party, routing procurement profits to a non-cooperative jurisdiction without real personnel, premises, risk, or board authority in Switzerland
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: General anti-abuse conversion of the company's income stream, denial of DTA benefits, deemed constructive dividend subject to 35% withholding tax, and administrative fines up to CHF 250,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pierced under Art. 52 DBG for unpaid withholding taxes and corporate tax; deregistration from the commercial register, personal travel restrictions, and criminal prosecution for tax concealment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting government direct wire and diplomatic LC proceeds without proper end-user verification, KYC, or required SECO/State Secretariat for Economic Affairs and Federal Agent for Export Control licensing for armored military-tactical vehicles
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to CHF 500,000, confiscation of transaction proceeds, mandatory referral to the Money Laundering Reporting Office of Switzerland, and revocation of the Federal War Material Act manufacturing and trading license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal exposure under Art. 305bis/305ter Swiss Criminal Code, imprisonment up to 5 years, personal asset freeze, forfeiture, and permanent exclusion from defense-industry governance positions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing sales of all-terrain military tactical vehicles to a related offshore distributor while failing to maintain documented comparables, contractual substance, or economic risk allocation, shifting profit to a low-tax territory
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax audit adjustment of the transfer price to arm's-length value, supplementary tax assessment plus 4% default interest, penalty of up to 10% of the additional tax, and hidden profit distribution subject to 35% withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the additional withholding tax through statutory veil-lifting, subject to criminal aiding-and-abetting charges, Swiss banking disclosure orders, and forfeiture of personal assets in favor of the tax authorities
